_comment: Plugin manager, native emtk window. Drawn by emtk.view_form over PluginManagerModel (gui/model.py): 'registered' is the left window (actions, the plugin table, the Show disabled switch, the status line), 'selected' the right one (details, switches, window-state choices, the dependency table), 'dialog' the in-app confirm / notice / rename dialog the Qt tool asked with message boxes, 'icon' the icon panel. The details text is Markdown and the icon preview an image, both drawn by gui/app.py (a spec cannot draw them).
title: Plugins

sections.title: Installed plugins
sections.name: registered
sections.description: Every plugin ChiSurf discovered, from the shipped tree and from your own plugin directory.
Save or revert the plugin settings, rescan the plugin folders, install or uninstall a plugin.

buttons.label: Save
buttons.description: Write the plugin settings. Menu changes take effect after a restart.

buttons.label: Revert
buttons.description: Discard every change made since the last save (asks first).

buttons.label: Rescan
buttons.description: Walk the plugin folders again and rebuild the list, in the background.

buttons.label: Install…
buttons.description: Install a plugin from a .zip archive (or, if you cancel that, from a folder) into your personal plugin directory.

buttons.label: Uninstall
buttons.description: Delete the selected plugin (asks first). Only plugins you installed yourself can be removed; built-in ones are switched off instead.

sections.description: Reorder, rename or re-icon the selected plugin, open its folder, copy or export the table.

buttons.label: Move up
buttons.description: Move the selected plugin earlier in the menus.

buttons.label: Move down
buttons.description: Move the selected plugin later in the menus.

buttons.label: Rename…
buttons.description: Change the name this plugin shows in the menus. Edits the plugin's manifest, which is the field the menus actually read.

buttons.label: Icon…
buttons.description: Choose, generate or clear the icon shown beside this plugin.

buttons.label: Open folder
buttons.description: Open the selected plugin's directory in the file browser.

buttons.label: Copy
buttons.description: Copy the rows the table shows now, with the column headers, to the clipboard as tab-separated text.

buttons.label: Export CSV
buttons.description: Write the rows and columns the table shows now to a CSV file.

sections.description: One row per plugin. Click a header to sort, click it again to reverse; type in the filter box to keep rows containing the text in any column; right click a header to choose columns (Id, Optional, Source, Toolbar and Window state start hidden). 'Requires' is what must load first; 'Required by' is what breaks if you switch it off.

columns.title: Plugin
columns.tooltip: The name shown in the menus.

columns.title: Version
columns.tooltip: The version from the plugin's manifest.

columns.title: Status
columns.tooltip: enabled, disabled, library, cli only, or a maturity flag.

columns.title: Requires
columns.tooltip: Loaded before this plugin: a module-level import.

columns.title: Required by
columns.tooltip: These stop working if this plugin is switched off.

columns.title: Optional
columns.tooltip: Reached only after startup, from a button press or a guarded import.

columns.title: Id
columns.tooltip: The manifest id; settings are keyed by it.

columns.title: Source
columns.tooltip: built-in, or user for a plugin in your own directory.

columns.title: Toolbar
columns.tooltip: yes when the plugin is pinned to the main toolbar.

columns.title: Window state
columns.tooltip: Whether the plugin's window remembers its size and position.

sections.label: Show disabled plugins
sections.description: Include switched-off plugins in the table. Off, they are hidden entirely.
How many plugins were found, how many are off, how many need attention, and whether anything is unsaved.

sections.title: Selected plugin
sections.name: selected
sections.description: What the selected plugin is, whether it is offered, and how it is wired to the others.
What the selected plugin is, where it lives, and how it is wired to the others.

sections.label: Disabled
sections.description: Switch this plugin off. If other plugins require it, you are told which before the change sticks.

sections.label: Show in main toolbar
sections.description: Pin this plugin to the main window toolbar.

sections.label: Remember window state
sections.description: Whether this one plugin's window reopens where you left it. 'Plugin default' defers to its manifest and the global setting below.

sections.label: Window state (all plugins)
sections.description: Whether plugin windows remember their size and position. 'Plugin default' lets each manifest decide.

sections.label: GUI runtime
sections.description: Which interface plugins open in: the emtk version, the Qt version, or whichever the plugin prefers (Automatic).

sections.title: Dependencies
sections.description: Every dependency edge touching this plugin, in both directions, with the state of the plugin at the other end.

columns.title: Plugin
columns.tooltip: The plugin at the other end of the edge.

columns.title: Relation
columns.tooltip: requires, optional, required by or optional for.

columns.title: Bound
columns.tooltip: The version bound the manifest asks for; any when it asks for none.

columns.title: Installed
columns.tooltip: The version of that plugin that is installed; a dash when it is not.

columns.title: Status
columns.tooltip: The state of that plugin: enabled, disabled, missing and so on.

sections.title: Plugin Manager
sections.name: dialog
sections.description: Asks before discarding changes, installing or deleting a plugin, and takes the new menu name.
What will happen if you confirm.

sections.label: Menu name
sections.description: The new leaf name of the plugin's menu entry; the menu path is kept.
Confirm or cancel.

buttons.label: OK
buttons.description: Do it.

buttons.label: Cancel
buttons.description: Leave everything as it is.

sections.title: Icon
sections.name: icon
sections.description: Choose, generate or clear one plugin's icon.
The icon as it appears beside the plugin.

sections.label: Image
sections.description: Path to an image to use as this plugin's icon. PNG is copied as is; other formats are rendered onto a square canvas.
Pick, write, generate, edit or clear the icon.

buttons.label: Choose…
buttons.description: Pick an image file from disk.

buttons.label: Use
buttons.description: Write the chosen image as this plugin's icon.

buttons.label: Generate…
buttons.description: Ask the configured AI provider for an icon, in the background.

buttons.label: Edit
buttons.description: Open the icon in the system image editor.

buttons.label: Clear
buttons.description: Remove the icon file and the manifest reference (asks first).

sections.label: Provider
sections.description: Which image provider to ask. The API key is taken from AI Settings.

sections.label: Endpoint
sections.description: Base URL of the provider's API.

sections.label: Image model
sections.description: Image model to request.
What the last icon action did.
Close the icon panel.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.description: Close the panel; a changed icon rescans the plugins.
